title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: no one foreseen persevering to whom God has not yet decreed the gift
pass_a_gloss: Eighthly, we argue thus. No one was ever foreseen as having persevering faith, to whom God has not yet decreed to impart this excellent gift. But if God has already decreed to give perseverance to Peter, Paul, or any singular man; it is manifest that he is already elected and ordained by God to life. For in the very gift of perseverance is situated an infallible ordination to eternal life. Little therefore is it agreeable to reason that God himself should elect singular persons to life from foresight of his own gift, which he never gave, or decreed to give, except to those whom he antecedently destined to eternal life.
pass_b_english: Eighth argument: no one was ever foreseen as having persevering faith unless God had already decreed to give that excellent gift. If God has decreed perseverance for Peter, Paul, or any particular person, that one is already elected and ordained to life — for the gift of perseverance itself carries an infallible ordination to eternal life. It is hardly reasonable that God should elect particular persons to life by foresight of his own gift, which he never gives or decrees to give except to those he has already destined to eternal life.
source_text: Octavo, sic argumentamur. Nemo unquam praevisus est ut habens fidem perseverantem, cui Deus nondum decrevit hoc eximium donum impertire. Quod si Deus jam decreverit Petro, Paulo, aut cuilibet homini singulari dare perseverantiam; manifestum est illum jam esse a Deo ad vitam electum et ordinatum. Nam in ipso perseverantiae dono sita est infallibilis ad vitam aeternam ordinatio. Parum igitur rationi consentaneum est, ipsum Deum eligere singulares personas ad vitam ex praevisione proprii sui doni, quod nunquam dedit, aut dare decrevit, nisi illis quos antecedenter ad vitam aeternam destinavit.
